  1313	#### FR-93: Guaranteed date, extension, and shutdown
  1314	
  1315	Every buyer sees the guaranteed date on the store listing, at purchase, and in the parent area. The date is at least 24 months after public launch and can only move later. Realizes UJ-5.
  1316	
  1317	**Consequences (testable):**
  1318	- Each January, the date moves one year later if trailing 6-month net revenue is at least twice the server and operations cost. The new date reaches devices through the service configuration (FR-94).
  1319	- If server talk will end, the parent area announces it at least 6 months before the guaranteed date, and opted-in parents also get an email (FR-75). After the end, Pip continues in basic mode.
  1320	- On the server tier, the unlock is not sold once less than 12 months remain before the guaranteed date.
  1321	- The date is set before the first early-access sale, at least 24 months after the planned public launch. If public launch slips, the date moves later, so it stays at least 24 months after the actual launch.
  1322	- Every protocol version used by a shipped server-tier app remains supported until the guaranteed date. An old app may be excluded only for a documented security risk that makes continued server-tier use unsafe and cannot be safely mitigated while supporting it. A compatible security update must be available without another purchase on that app's supported Android devices; restore preserves the unlock and updating preserves pet state. The parent area explains the update and next step; the child sees resting ears, and basic mode continues. Cost, ordinary maintenance, model changes and planned version retirement never qualify. An emergency with no compatible update is an unmet guarantee, escalated to the product owner, not a new shutdown exception.
  1323	
  1324	#### FR-94: Service configuration
  1325	
  1326	Online devices attempt the service-configuration check at most daily and at least once every 30 days when connectivity permits. The signed global configuration carries the guaranteed date, parent notices, and content and list versions. Linked devices also perform the link check; signed per-device items in its response deliver web unlinks and record-deletion notices.
  1327	
  1328	**Consequences (testable):**
  1329	- A configuration that fails its signature check is ignored.
  1330	- The global configuration carries no device credential. The linked-device check sends only its single-use link-check value and allowed protocol metadata, never the server credential or link ID `[ASSUMPTION: CQ-32]`.
  1331	- If a device cannot fetch, or a fetched file fails validation, it keeps the last good file. Fetch age alone never changes the child view. Caps, consent, security restrictions and the guaranteed date still apply on their own terms. With no good file, the device uses the bundled defaults; it never assumes an extension it has not received.
  1332	
  1333	### 4.14 The on-device brain
  1334	
  1335	**Description:** On capable devices, the model is downloaded once after the unlock, then works without a network, and keeps working if our servers stop. The download is the parent's action, never a surprise, and the child keeps playing meanwhile.
  1336	
  1337	#### FR-95: Model download
  1338	
  1339	After the unlock on the on-device tier, a parent starts the model download. It uses Wi-Fi by default (mobile data only if the parent chooses), survives interruptions, and resumes where it stopped. Pip stays in basic mode meanwhile. Realizes UJ-3.
  1340	
  1341	**Consequences (testable):**
  1342	- The download keeps running while the app is in the background, with a neutral notification addressed to the parent when notifications are allowed (mechanism: addendum §2.9).
  1343	- Models come from storage we control. The storage provider works under an agreement, and its access logs are kept for at most 7 days `[ASSUMPTION]`.
  1344	
  1345	#### FR-96: Model integrity
  1346	
  1347	A downloaded model is used only after its checksum matches a signed manifest; a mismatch deletes the file and restarts the download.

item.text:
The kid should see the usual Pip experience: settings being over a month old must not by itself change the child view. The phone keeps the last valid settings, or bundled defaults if none exist; caps, consent, security restrictions and the guaranteed date still apply, and an unseen extension cannot be assumed. If a separate condition stops talk, Pip shows folded “resting ears” and keeps playing with basic-mode features; the cause is explained only to the parent.
